reviews.title: Does the job, temp display is kinda neat
reviews.comment: Picked this up to replace the stock cooler on my Ryzen 5 build. Installation was pretty straightforward - took maybe 20 minutes following the instructions. The mounting hardware worked fine with my AM4 socket. The temp display on the top is actually kind of cool. It's not essential or anything, but it's nice to glance at my temps without opening monitoring software. Seems accurate compared to what HWiNFO shows. Cooling performance is good. My CPU sits around 35-40°C idle and hits maybe 65-70°C under load, which is a big improvement over the stock cooler that was pushing 80°C. Not silent but way quieter than I expected. You can hear it if the room is quiet, but it's not annoying. The thermal paste was pre-applied which saved me a step, though I probably would've used my own if I'd known. Worked fine though. Only complaint is the temp display is bright - if your PC is in your bedroom it might bug you at night. I just turn my monitor off so whatever. For the price this is solid. Keeps things cool, looks decent, and the temp display is a nice touch. Would buy again if I needed another budget cooler.

reviews.title: Minimalistic design, silent FDB fan & ultra low idle temps. LED readout requires software running
reviews.comment: I installed this cooler on my dad’s office PC that's running an older Intel 10th gen i3. Installation was the easiest I’ve ever done for any cooler as all I had to do was just go by the single page illustration showing 6 simple steps. I didn’t even need to look up the socket number once I got the rods on the bracket to fit the holes on the motherboard. The cooler even comes with thermal paste pre-applied, and it also includes a full tube of paste. The cooler attaches to the bracket with only two main screws, but once tightened, it feels rock solid with zero movement. I like the simple, all black, minimalistic look of both the cooler and the fan. The fan has a premium build quality with fluid dynamic bearings and spins virtually silently at under 700 RPM when sitting idle on the desktop. The CPU temp at idle is literally just a few degrees above room temp at around 27C. I didn’t bother testing maximum temp under full CPU load since this is just an office machine, but based on its idle performance at low fan speeds, I’m sure it'd perform just as well on this i3. The temp readout on the cooler is a neat feature and is very responsive and accurate. However, it does require its software to be running constantly. When I exit out of the software, the led simply turns off entirely. This isn’t much of an issue since the software is very light on resource and mostly sits at 0% CPU usage (though I've seen it occasionally spike to 3 to 5%). As far as I know, this software requirement is common for all CPU coolers with LED temp readouts. Considering the built-in temp readout LED feature, the premium build quality, and the virtually silent fluid dynamic fan, the current price seems fair. But if you don’t care about the CPU temp readout LED, I’d recommend their A620 PRO SE that has 6 heat pipes, dual tower and dual fans, which can actually be found for less than the current price of this cooler here on amazon.
